claims.explanation: Thiocolchicoside is a colchicine-site tubulin binder whose anticancer selectivity is best explained by the microtubule/NF-κB axis rather than by GABA receptor expression, since the annotated GABA targets are not plausibly linked to the killing pattern. Lines with intact apoptotic and NF-κB-dependent survival signaling (TP53 wild-type or functional, low BCL2/XIAP, high NFKB1/RELA) are most sensitive, while lines with constitutive survival pathway activation (PIK3CA/PTEN loss, high BCL2) are protected. The observed enrichment of TP53 mutations among sensitive lines is consistent with mitotic catastrophe/apoptosis dependence on p53 signaling.

Thiocolchicoside downregulates Bcl-2; high BCL2 expression blunts apoptosis

Thiocolchicoside inhibits NF-κB; tumors with high NF-κB dependence are more affected
NF-κB pathway activity is the proposed anticancer target of thiocolchicoside
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched in the least-affected set, suggesting PI3K survival signaling protects
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival and appears in several resistant lines
BRAF-mutant melanomas are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven mitotic vulnerability
KRAS-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set, consistent with MAPK-dependent survival
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are enriched in the least-affected set
Tubulin-binding drugs require adequate tubulin target; high TUBB expression may increase sensitivity
Annotated GABA receptor target; expression may mediate non-cytotoxic effects but is weak evidence
